title: The Crow and the Pitcher
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, on a long, hot summer's day, the fields were dry, and the little streams had shrunk away to nothing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A little crow had been flying for hours and hours, and she was very, very thirsty.

lines.speaker: crow
lines.speech: [weary, a little hoarse] Oh, I'm so thirsty. If only I could find a drop of water.
lines.text: Oh, I'm so thirsty. If only I could find a drop of water.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Just then, she spotted something in a cottage garden below. A tall clay pitcher, standing by the garden wall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She flew down, and peeked inside. There was water! But only a little, right at the very bottom.

lines.speaker: crow
lines.speech: [hopeful, then dismayed] Water! Oh... but it's so far down.
lines.text: Water! Oh... but it's so far down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She pushed her beak in as far as it would go. But she could not reach it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She tried to tip the pitcher over. But it was far too heavy.

lines.speaker: crow
lines.speech: [thinking, determined] Hmm. There must be a way. Let me think.
lines.text: Hmm. There must be a way. Let me think.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then she noticed the little pebbles lying on the garden path. And she had an idea!

lines.speaker: crow
lines.text: I know!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She picked up a pebble in her beak, and dropped it into the pitcher. Plip!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then another. Plop! And another, and another.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pebble by pebble, the water rose higher, and higher.

lines.speaker: crow
lines.speech: [delighted] It's working! Just a few more...
lines.text: It's working! Just a few more...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Until at last, the cool water came right up to the top.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crow dipped her beak, and drank, and drank, until she was not thirsty any more.

lines.speaker: crow
lines.speech: [happy, satisfied sigh] Ahh. Little by little does the trick!
lines.text: Ahh. Little by little does the trick!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And so, when something seems too hard, remember. A little patience, and a clever idea, can always find a way.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: As the sun went down, the crow flew home to her nest in the old elm tree.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She tucked her head beneath her soft black wing, and the evening breeze sang her to sleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The moon rose over the quiet garden, and the stars came out to keep watch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
